title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
appbay.yaml is the metadata file that augments a Docker Compose project with Appbay features. It is placed alongside docker-compose.yml in an app directory under $APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps/<name>/.
The file is optional. If absent, the app is treated as a plain Compose project with default scope values.

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Scope fields
These fields control where the app belongs in the organizational model.









Field
Type
Default
Description




namespace
string
(none)
Deployment identity, flat and dot-delimited (uom.sim). Enters container, network, DNS-alias and edge-fragment names. No default — absence means “decided at deploy time”.


project
—
—
Removed in RFC-001 §4 — use namespace. A non-default value is a parse error.


environment
—
—
Removed in RFC-001 §4 — use namespace. ⚠️ environment: inside a service is Compose’s own field and is unaffected.


collection
string[]
(none)
Operational groupings for batch operations. Multi-valued.


operator
string
(none)
Reserved for future multi-node placement. Accepted and ignored in v1 — everything runs locally.


shared_network
string[]
["appbay_shared"]
Shared network(s) that exposed services join.


tags
Record<string, string>
(none)
Arbitrary key-value pairs for UI filtering and bulk operations. No scoping semantics.



namespace: homelab.prod
collection: [media, gpu-apps]
operator: local
shared_network: [appbay_shared]
tags:
  tier: media
  team: infra

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Upstream section
Configures how a stock upstream Compose file is ingested without modification.









Field
Type
Default
Description




upstream.source
string
(none)
Path to the upstream compose file, relative to the app directory.


upstream.services.exclude
string[]
(none)
Service names to remove from the upstream compose (e.g., remove nginx when using Traefik).


upstream.expose
ExposeEntry[]
(none)
Services to alias on shared networks for external access.




ExposeEntry
Three shorthand forms are accepted:








Form
Example
Effect




String
"api"
Expose service api on all shared_network entries


Alias map
{ web: "dify-web" }
Expose with a custom alias (key = alias, value = service name)


Full object
{ service: "api", networks: [...] }
Explicit service name and network list



upstream:
  source: jellyfin-upstream/docker-compose.yml
  services:
    exclude: [nginx]
  expose:
    - jellyfin                           # shorthand string form
    # or:
    - service: jellyfin
      networks: [appbay_shared]          # full object form

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Overrides section
Static Compose overrides keyed by original service name. These are deep-merged into the upstream compose output.
overrides:
  jellyfin:
    environment:
      - TZ=${{project.TZ}}
    volumes:
      - jellyfin_config:/config
      - /mnt/media:/media:ro

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Overlays section
Conditional Compose fragments applied when peer apps are active. Each overlay has a when clause and a services block.








Field
Type
Description




overlays[].when
string[] or { any: string[] }
Condition for activation. Array = AND (all must be active). { any: [...] } = OR (at least one active).


overlays[].services
Record<string, any>
Compose service fragments to merge when the condition is met.



overlays:
  # AND: both ollama and whisper must be active
  - when: [ollama, whisper]
    services:
      webui:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434
          - WHISPER_URL=http://whisper_web:9000

  # OR: either postgres or mysql
  - when:
      any: [postgres, mysql]
    services:
      app:
        environment:
          - DB_AVAILABLE=true

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Traits section (app-level)
App-level traits apply to the entire app. Declared at the top level.
traits:
  - type: backup
    schedule: "0 2 * * *"
    retention: 7
  - type: auth
    enabled: true

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Services section (service-level traits)
Service-level traits apply to individual Compose services. Do not re-list services from the compose file – only reference them for trait assignment.
services:
  jellyfin:
    traits:
      - type: ingress
        host: "media.${{project.DOMAIN}}"
        port: 8096
        exposure: both
      - type: gpu
        variant: nvidia

title: appbay.yaml Schema Reference
text:
Builds section
Images this app builds from source, rather than pulls. Keyed by service name.
builds:
  web:
    image: myapp/web:1.4.0
    pull_if_present: docker.io/myapp/web:1.4.0









Field
Type
Required
Description




image
string
yes
Tag to build and pin the service’s image: to


when
object
no
Conditions controlling whether the build runs


verify
object
no
Post-build verification


pull_if_present
string
no
Pull this reference instead, when it already exists



Appbay hoists the build: it builds ahead of the deploy, pins image: to the tag above, and strips build: from the rendered output. That last part is the point, not tidiness — a rendered compose still carrying build: puts an implicit image build inside compose up, which on Podman’s compatibility API is the least-tested path in the stack. After hoisting, the render is purely “run this image”.

title: CLI Command Reference
text: The Appbay CLI is a single compiled binary built with Bun. It directly imports @appbay/core and operates entirely offline — it does not use a tRPC client or require the Appbay server to be running. Commands that deploy containers invoke docker compose directly.

title: CLI Command Reference
text: The Appbay CLI is a single compiled binary built with Bun. It directly imports @appbay/core and operates entirely offline — it does not use a tRPC client or require the Appbay server to be running. Commands that deploy containers invoke docker compose directly.

title: CLI Command Reference
text:
Global flags







Flag
Description




--help
Show help for any command


--version
Print CLI version


--server <url>
Override server URL (default: http://localhost:3000)


--token <token>
Override auth token (alternative to APPBAY_TOKEN env var)

title: CLI Command Reference
text:
Commands

appbay setup
The guided path, and the one most people should start with: it runs init, creates the secret vault, and brings up the edge, in order, asking only for what it cannot infer.
appbay setup --domain home.lan
appbay setup --domain example.com --email you@example.com --ingress-provider caddy --yes
appbay setup --status








Flag
Default
Description




--domain <domain>
(prompted)
Base domain for ingress routing


--project <name>
(prompted)
Project name


--email <email>
(prompted)
ACME email, for Let’s Encrypt certificates


--ingress-provider <p>
traefik
Edge to install: traefik or caddy


--yes
false
Non-interactive: accept all defaults


--status
—
Report what is already set up, and change nothing


--reset
—
Tear down system apps and remove generated configs



⚠️ The administrator setup creates is the edge administrator, which guards apps behind the reverse proxy — and since RFC-001 §1 that is the SAME account that signs in to the web control plane, which no longer has one of its own. It needs the authp/admin role to reach the control plane. See Credentials — the two are deliberately separate and are never synchronised.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = a step failed.


appbay install
Install an app from the catalog into $APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps/<name>/.
appbay install jellyfin
appbay install nextcloud --set ADMIN_USER=me --set TZ=Europe/Berlin
appbay install adminer --as adminer-staging      # a second copy








Flag
Default
Description




--set <pairs...>
—
Input values as KEY=VALUE, repeatable


--as <name>
the catalog name
Install under a different app name


--force
false
Overwrite an app of the same name


--no-validate
false
Skip post-install validation



--as splits the catalog lookup from the install location, which is what makes a second copy possible: without it both were the same value, so installing an entry twice overwrote it.
⚠️ Not the same axis as namespace:. A namespace disambiguates two deployments of one installed app; --as gives you two installations, each with its own directory, manifest and config. Use --as when the copies should differ in what they are, namespace: when they differ only in where they run.
Installing copies the upstream files unmodified and writes an appbay.yaml beside them. Nothing is deployed until you run appbay up.


appbay catalog
Browse and manage catalog sources.
appbay catalog list
appbay catalog search media
appbay catalog info jellyfin
appbay catalog add-source https://github.com/you/your-catalog
appbay catalog update


appbay shell · appbay exec · appbay run
Reach into a running app.
appbay shell jellyfin                      # interactive shell in the service container
appbay exec jellyfin -- ls /config          # run a command in the running container
appbay run jellyfin -- /bin/backup.sh       # one-off command in a fresh container
shell and exec require the app to be running; run starts a container for the command and removes it afterwards.


appbay init-system
Bootstrap a fresh host to run Appbay: installs the container runtime and sets up ownership and access for the Appbay tree. Written for RHEL-family hosts, where the defaults differ enough to matter.
sudo appbay init-system                     # --owner service (default)
sudo appbay init-system --owner operator
--owner service creates a no-login system service account, which is the right choice for a homelab or worklab box. --owner operator uses your own account instead.


appbay init
Scaffold the $APPBAY_HOME directory structure and seed system app definitions.
appbay init
appbay init --dir /opt/appbay
appbay init --project homelab --domain homelab.example.com --yes








Flag
Default
Description




--dir <path>
~/.appbay
Override $APPBAY_HOME location — persisted, see below


--project <name>
(prompted)
Name of the default project


--domain <name>
(prompted)
Base domain for ingress routing


--yes
false
Non-interactive: accept all defaults



Creates: etc/apps/, etc/projects/, etc/presets/, var/lib/renders/, var/lib/state/, var/log/. Seeds system app definitions if absent.






Warning--dir changes where every later command looks



--dir is not scoped to this one run: it writes the path to ~/.config/appbay/home, so every subsequent appbay invocation on this account resolves there until you change it. Undo it with appbay home clear, or repoint with appbay home set <path>.
To initialise a throwaway install without touching that default — what a test or a journey script wants — set the environment variable instead, which init honours as a runtime override and deliberately does not persist:
APPBAY_HOME=/tmp/scratch/home appbay init --project t --domain t.local --yes


Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = filesystem error.


appbay server start
Start the Appbay server as a Docker Compose stack.
appbay server start
appbay server start --open



Flag
Default
Description




--open
false
Open the web UI in a browser after start



Creates appbay_shared network, starts the appbay-server container, waits for health check, prints the server URL.
Exit codes: 0 = server healthy, 1 = start failed, 2 = health check timeout.


appbay server stop
Stop the server container.
appbay server stop
Exit codes: 0 = stopped, 1 = error.


appbay server status
Check whether the Appbay server is running. Prints the server URL and start time if running, or a “not running” message if it is not.
appbay server status
Exit codes: 0 = always (status is informational).


appbay up
Deploy one or more apps.
appbay up jellyfin
appbay up ollama webui tts
appbay up --collection ai-stack
appbay up --all



Flag
Default
Description




--collection <name>
(none)
Deploy all apps in a collection


--all
false
Deploy all discovered apps



Runs the full pipeline: compile, apply overlays, write renders, and bring up via docker compose up -d.
Exit codes: 0 = deployed, 1 = compile or deploy error.


appbay apply
Compile and review a plan, then deploy with explicit confirmation. Separates compile and deploy for review workflows.
appbay apply jellyfin
appbay apply ollama webui --dry-run
appbay apply jellyfin --yes
appbay apply --all --yes



Flag
Default
Description




--dry-run
false
Show the plan without applying


--yes
false
Skip confirmation prompt and deploy immediately


--all
false
Apply all discovered apps



Exit codes: 0 = applied (or dry run complete), 1 = compile or deploy error.


appbay down
Stop one or more running apps.
appbay down jellyfin
appbay down webui tts
appbay down --all



Flag
Default
Description




--all
false
Stop all discovered apps



Exit codes: 0 = stopped, 1 = error.


appbay delete
Remove an app definition and stop its containers.
appbay delete myapp --keep-volumes --force



Flag
Default
Description




--keep-volumes
false
Keep Docker volumes after deletion


--force
false
Skip confirmation prompt (required to proceed)



Without --force, the command exits with an error and instructions. Runs docker compose down (with -v unless --keep-volumes) before removing the app definition directory.
Exit codes: 0 = deleted, 1 = not found or confirmation required.


appbay restart
Restart one or more apps.
appbay restart jellyfin
appbay restart webui tts
appbay restart --all



Flag
Default
Description




--all
false
Restart all discovered apps



Exit codes: 0 = restarted, 1 = error.


appbay pull
Pull the latest Docker images for one or more apps.
appbay pull jellyfin
appbay pull ollama webui
appbay pull --all



Flag
Default
Description




--all
false
Pull images for all discovered apps



Uses the rendered compose file if available, otherwise falls back to the source compose.
Exit codes: 0 = all pulls succeeded, 1 = one or more failed.


appbay compile
Run the compiler pipeline without deploying.
appbay compile jellyfin
appbay compile jellyfin webui
appbay compile              # compiles all discovered apps








Flag
Default
Description




--output <dir>
var/lib/renders/
Write rendered output to a custom directory



Runs the full compile pipeline and writes rendered compose and auxiliary files. Available offline (no server needed).
Exit codes: 0 = compiled, 1 = error.


appbay validate
Validate app definitions against Zod schemas.
appbay validate jellyfin
appbay validate --all
Reports errors with file paths, field names, and expected types. Available offline.
Exit codes: 0 = valid, 1 = validation errors found.


appbay eject
Export a fully standalone Compose project.
appbay eject jellyfin
appbay eject jellyfin --output ./exported/



Flag
Default
Description




--output <path>
./appbay-eject/<app>/
Output directory



Produces a directory with docker-compose.yml and .env that can be run with docker compose up without Appbay. Available offline.
Exit codes: 0 = ejected, 1 = error.


appbay status
Show app configuration and metadata. Available offline.
appbay status
appbay status jellyfin
appbay status jellyfin --json



Flag
Description




--json
Output as JSON



Without an app name, shows a summary table of all discovered apps (name, services count, traits count, errors). With an app name, shows full detail: directory, project, environment, services (with service-level traits), app-level traits, overlays, and upstream configuration.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = app not found.


appbay logs
Show or stream app logs.
appbay logs jellyfin
appbay logs jellyfin redis --follow
appbay logs jellyfin --tail 100








Flag
Default
Description




-f, --follow
false
Stream logs in real time


--tail <n>
(Docker default)
Number of lines to show from the end



The optional second positional argument filters to a specific service within the app.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = error.


appbay doctor
Run prerequisite and health checks.
appbay doctor
Checks: Docker connectivity, Compose version, server health, disk space, system app status.
Exit codes: 0 = all checks passed, 1 = one or more checks failed.


appbay secrets init
Initialize the local secrets vault. Auto-generates a master password if none provided.
appbay secrets init
appbay secrets init --password mypassword


appbay secrets set
Store a secret in the vault. Key format: KEY for default scope, APP/KEY for app-scoped.
appbay secrets set DB_PASSWORD myvalue
appbay secrets set kestra/DB_PASSWORD myvalue
Warns if the secret already exists, with database-specific guidance.


appbay secrets get
Retrieve a secret value from the vault.
appbay secrets get DB_PASSWORD
appbay secrets get kestra/DB_PASSWORD


appbay secrets delete
Delete a secret from the vault.
appbay secrets delete DB_PASSWORD
appbay secrets delete kestra/DB_PASSWORD


appbay secrets vault
List all secrets stored in the vault, grouped by scope. Shows metadata only — never values.
appbay secrets vault
appbay secrets vault --scope kestra


appbay secrets scan
Discover secret-like env vars in an app’s compose and .env files. Suggests vault URI mappings for unmanaged secrets.
appbay secrets scan kestra


appbay secrets import
Scan an app and auto-create vault entries for unmanaged secret-like variables.
appbay secrets import kestra
appbay secrets import kestra --dry-run


appbay secrets export
Export vault contents to a KeePass .kdbx file.
# `secrets export` was removed with the kdbx work; use `appbay secrets list`
appbay secrets list


appbay secrets import-kdbx
Import secrets from a KeePass .kdbx file into the vault.
appbay secrets import-kdbx secrets.kdbx --password mypass


appbay secrets check
Verify that all secret URI references across all apps can be resolved.
appbay secrets check


appbay secrets list
List secret URI references for an app (or all apps). Prints URIs only — never values.
appbay secrets list
appbay secrets list jellyfin


appbay edge users list
List Caddy Security local edge users.
appbay edge users list


appbay edge users create
Create a Caddy Security local edge user.
appbay edge users create newuser --email user@example.com --roles user
appbay edge users create newuser --email user@example.com --generate --reveal


appbay edge users reset-password
Reset a Caddy Security local edge user’s password.
appbay edge users reset-password username


appbay admin — retired
RFC-001 §1 removed AppBay’s own accounts. The control plane is a stack behind the Caddy Security edge like any other app, so the account that signs in to AppBay is an edge user:
appbay edge users reset-password alice --generate --reveal
Running appbay admin prints this and exits non-zero, so a script that still calls it fails rather than appearing to succeed.






ImportantOne store now, and a role instead of a second password



There is no longer a separate credential domain for the control plane. What distinguishes it is the role: its edge route carries an admin-only policy (authp/admin), narrower than an app’s default, because it is the one stack that can reach the container runtime socket. So “can open Grafana” still does not imply “can reconfigure the installation”.




appbay rebuild-cache
Regenerate the SQLite metadata cache from filesystem state.
appbay rebuild-cache
Deletes the existing appbay.db, creates a fresh database with Drizzle migrations, and populates all tables from filesystem sources. Available offline.
Exit codes: 0 = rebuilt, 1 = error.


appbay update
Check for and apply CLI and system app updates.
appbay update
appbay update --check
appbay update --system-only



Flag
Default
Description




--check
false
Check for updates without applying


--system-only
false
Only pull system app Docker images



Exit codes: 0 = updated, 1 = pull failed, 2 = restart failed.


appbay list
List all discovered apps. Available offline.
appbay list
appbay list --json







Flag
Description




--all
Include apps with discovery errors (default: all apps shown anyway)


--json
Output as JSON array



Reads from $APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps/ and shows each app’s name, project, environment, whether an appbay.yaml exists, and the compose filename. Does not require Docker or the server to be running.
Exit codes: 0 = success.


appbay ps
Show container runtime status for apps. Runs docker compose ps against rendered compose files.
appbay ps
appbay ps jellyfin
appbay ps jellyfin redis
appbay ps --json



Flag
Default
Description




--all
false
Include apps without rendered compose files


--json
false
Output as JSON



Prefers the rendered compose file in var/lib/renders/; falls back to the source compose.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = docker compose failed or no apps found.


appbay config
Get or set configuration values in an app’s appbay.yaml. Uses dot-separated key paths.
appbay config jellyfin                          # show all config
appbay config jellyfin upstream.source          # read a single key
appbay config jellyfin upstream.source my-app  # set a value
Values are auto-coerced: "true" → boolean, "42" → number, everything else stays string.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = app or key not found.


appbay env
Manage environment variables in an app’s .env file ($APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps/<app>/.env).
appbay env jellyfin               # list all variables
appbay env jellyfin DB_HOST       # get a variable
appbay env jellyfin DB_HOST db    # set a variable
appbay env jellyfin DB_HOST --delete  # delete a variable



Flag
Default
Description




--list
false
List all variables


--delete
false
Delete the specified variable



Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = app not found or key not found.


appbay presets
Manage named app selection presets. Presets save which apps are selected together for quick recall. Stored as YAML in $APPBAY_HOME/etc/presets/.
appbay presets save ai-dev --apps "ollama,webui,whisper"
appbay presets load ai-dev
appbay presets list
appbay presets delete ai-dev

appbay presets save <name>



Flag
Description




--apps <list>
Comma-separated app names to include


--description <desc>
Optional description





appbay presets load <name>
Prints the app list from the preset. Typically piped to appbay up:
appbay up $(appbay presets load ai-dev)


appbay presets list
List all saved presets with their app lists.


appbay presets delete <name>
Delete a preset by name.



appbay open
Open an app’s URL in the default browser.
appbay open jellyfin
Resolves the app’s ingress URL from the ingress trait configuration and opens it.
Exit codes: 0 = opened, 1 = no ingress configured.


appbay url
Print an app’s URL without opening the browser. Resolves the ingress trait or falls back to compose port mappings.
appbay url jellyfin
appbay url jellyfin --lan
appbay url jellyfin --internal



Flag
Description




--lan
Show the LAN address


--internal
Show the internal Docker network address



Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = app not found.


appbay version
Print the Appbay CLI version.
appbay version
Exit codes: 0 = always.


appbay home
Print, explain or repoint the resolved $APPBAY_HOME path.
appbay home                  # print the resolved path, and nothing else
appbay home --explain        # show every tier and which one wins
appbay home set <path>       # persist a new home for future commands
appbay home clear            # forget the persisted home
Bare appbay home prints only the path, so cd $(appbay home)/etc/apps keeps working.
Resolution order — the first tier with a value wins:








#
Tier
Set by




1
$APPBAY_HOME
the environment; a runtime override that always wins


2
/etc/appbay/config
appbay init-system (a host-level decision) — holds home: and nothing else


3
~/.config/appbay/home
appbay init --dir, or appbay home set


4
~/.appbay
built-in default









NoteWhy tier 2 is a file and not a systemd unit



RFC-001 proposed replacing it with Environment=APPBAY_HOME= in a unit. Measured on a real host, a unit’s environment reaches the processes systemd starts and nothing else: the service saw the home, an operator’s login shell saw nothing. Tier 2 serves that second case — an operator typing appbay … — which is precisely where a per-operator ~/.config/appbay/home would otherwise win. Deleting it made the CLI resolve a personal path over a service install.


--explain prints all four with the winner marked, and warns when the resolved path does not exist, has no etc/ (never initialised), or is a saved pointer under a temp directory that will not survive a reboot.
set writes tier 3 and refuses when tier 1 or 2 would shadow it — a saved path that a higher tier overrides is a setting that reports success and changes nothing. It also refuses a path that does not exist. --force overrides both refusals; when forced past a shadowing tier it says so rather than claiming the resolved home changed.
clear removes tier 3 and reports the tier now in force. Use it to undo an appbay init --dir that pointed at a directory you no longer want — including a throwaway one that has since been deleted.
Exit codes: 0 = printed, explained, set or cleared; 1 = set refused (shadowed by a higher tier, or the path is missing or not a directory).

text: The recommended deployment runs the Appbay control plane as a Docker Compose stack: an appbay-server container (Next.js + SQLite) with a read-only Docker socket mount. A single CLI binary manages the entire lifecycle.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Prerequisites

Docker Engine 24.0 or later with the Compose plugin (docker compose v2)
A Linux host (bare metal or VM). macOS and WSL2 work for development.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Quick start
# 1. Download the CLI binary (or build from source)
curl -fsSL https://get.appbay.dev | sh

# 2. Initialize the data directory
appbay init

# 3. Start the server stack
appbay server start
After appbay server start completes, open http://localhost:3000 to create your admin account.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
What appbay server start does
The command performs these steps in order:

Creates the shared network. Runs docker network create appbay_shared if it does not already exist. All deployed apps join this network so they can reach each other and the Traefik ingress.
Starts the appbay-server container. The Next.js standalone image mounts the Docker socket read-only and $APPBAY_HOME so it can read app definitions and write rendered output to the host filesystem. SQLite lives in a named volume (appbay-data) that persists across container rebuilds.
Waits for the health check. The CLI polls GET /api/trpc/health until the server responds with { status: "ok" }.
Prints the URL. Once healthy, the CLI prints the server URL and next steps.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Configuration

Environment variables








Variable
Default
Description




APPBAY_HOME
~/.appbay
Data directory on the host


APPBAY_PORT
3000
Port the server listens on


APPBAY_DB
/app/data/appbay.db
SQLite database path inside the container (backed by the appbay-data named volume)


DOCKER_HOST
(system default)
Docker API endpoint (uses mounted socket)





Volumes
The server compose stack defines two volume mounts:
volumes:
  # Host data directory -- app definitions, renders, state files
  - ${APPBAY_HOME:-~/.appbay}:${APPBAY_HOME:-/home/appbay/.appbay}
  # Named volume for SQLite (persistent across image upgrades)
  - appbay-data:/app/data
The host data directory is bind-mounted so that the server and CLI share the same filesystem view. The SQLite database uses a named volume because it is a rebuildable cache – if lost, appbay rebuild-cache regenerates it from the filesystem.


Networks
Two networks are created:

appbay_shared – external network that deployed apps join. Created as an external network so it persists independently of the server stack lifecycle.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
First-run setup
There is no setup mode and no admin account to create. RFC-001 §1 removed AppBay’s own accounts: the control plane authenticates through the Caddy Security edge, so whoever the edge identifies is who is signed in.
That makes the edge a prerequisite rather than an option. appbay server start writes the edge route and binds port 3000 to loopback in the same step, so the edge becomes the only way in:
appbay init --ingress-provider caddy
# set `domain:` in $APPBAY_HOME/etc/system.yaml
appbay server start          # -> https://appbay.<domain>, port 3000 on 127.0.0.1
Create the account that reaches it — admin-only, because the control plane can reach the container runtime socket:
appbay edge users create alice --generate --reveal
⚠️ Without an edge route the server does not fall back to a password. It has no way to authenticate anyone and refuses to serve, which the UI states explicitly. APPBAY_BIND=0.0.0.0 reopens the port but does not restore authentication.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Updating
Pull the latest server image and restart:
appbay update
This is equivalent to:
docker pull appbay/server:latest
docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up -d
The SQLite database persists in a named volume across image upgrades. If the new version includes schema migrations, Drizzle ORM runs them automatically on startup.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Stopping
appbay server stop
This stops the server container but preserves all data. Your deployed apps continue running independently.

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Backup
Back up the entire $APPBAY_HOME directory to preserve:

etc/ – app definitions, project configs, environment configs
var/lib/state/ – generated values, active app set, operator registry
var/lib/renders/ – rendered compose output (can be regenerated with appbay compile)

The SQLite database (the appbay-data named volume) does not need to be backed up separately. It is a metadata cache and can be rebuilt:
appbay rebuild-cache

title: Deploy as Compose App
text:
Troubleshooting
Server fails to start:
# Check container logs
docker logs appbay.server

# Verify the shared network exists
docker network ls | grep appbay_shared

# Run the doctor command
appbay doctor
Port conflict:
# Use a different port
APPBAY_PORT=8080 appbay server start
Permission denied on Docker socket:
Ensure your user is in the docker group, or run with appropriate permissions. The server container mounts /var/run/docker.sock read-only.

title: Deployment Overview
text:
How to choose
Use Compose if you want a production-ready install with minimal moving parts. The CLI binary handles bootstrapping the server container, creating the shared network, and running health checks. This is the default path documented throughout Appbay.
Use Native if you are developing Appbay itself, need to set breakpoints in the server code, or want to run the web UI in hot-reload mode. Native mode bypasses containerization of the control plane but still uses Docker Compose to manage your apps.

title: Deployment Overview
text:
Architecture summary
Regardless of deployment mode, the runtime architecture is the same:
Browser ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                                                           v
CLI ──── Direct import @appbay/core ──────────────────────┤
          (validate, compile, up, down, list, ...)         |
                                                    Appbay Server (Next.js + tRPC)
CLI ─ ─ ─ HTTP health check only ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ |
          (server start/stop/status)                       |
                                                           v
                                                    Docker Engine
                                              (socket mounted read-only)
The server container mounts the Docker socket read-only (/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro) and uses the docker CLI directly for container operations.






Note



The CLI operates entirely offline for all app management commands — it imports @appbay/core directly and does not require the Appbay server to be running. Only appbay server start/stop/status communicates with the server via HTTP health check. This means appbay validate, appbay compile, and appbay up all work in CI pipelines without a running server.

title: Deployment Overview
text:
Data directory
Both modes store all state under $APPBAY_HOME. Resolution order:

$APPBAY_HOME environment variable (explicit)
<repo>/.appbay/ if inside the Appbay monorepo (development)
~/.appbay (fallback for end users)

The data directory follows an FHS-inspired layout:
$APPBAY_HOME/
  etc/           # Authored configuration (app definitions, project config)
  var/lib/       # Runtime state (renders, SQLite cache, generated values)
  var/log/       # Logs
  bin/           # CLI binary
See Compose deployment or Native installation for step-by-step setup instructions. For hardened environments, see Production deployment.

title: Bootstrap Guide
text:
This guide walks a fresh host from “one compiled binary in hand” to a working Appbay deployment. It is written for both human and AI operators: every step has the exact command, the expected output, and the failure modes you are likely to hit.
The journey is:
binary in hand
   │
   ▼
appbay doctor        verify the environment can run Appbay
   │
   ▼
appbay init-system   (RHEL-family hosts) install Docker + appbay user
   │
   ▼
appbay init          scaffold $APPBAY_HOME, shared network, system apps
   │
   ▼
appbay setup         configure the edge (ingress + auth), deploy system apps
   │
   ▼
appbay up <app>      deploy your first app


Appbay ships as a single compiled binary — no Node.js, Bun, or other runtime is needed on the target machine. You need:








Requirement
Minimum
Check




Linux (x64/arm64) or macOS
—
uname -m


Docker or Podman
Docker 24.0+ / Podman 4.9+
docker --version


Compose v2
v2.23.1+
docker compose version



Compose v2.23.1+ is required because Appbay uses the configs resource with inline content, introduced in that release.


⚠️ AppBay does not install this for you. It consumes a runtime an administrator (or external automation) has already configured. AppBay never installs packages, invokes sudo, or mutates host services and firewall policy; appbay doctor reports what is missing and names the repair step, and stops there.
Measured on Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker 29.1.3, Compose v2.40.3):
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y docker.io docker-compose-v2
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"      # log out and back in for this to take effect
sudo systemctl enable --now docker



Measured on Ubuntu 24.04 (Podman 4.9.3, podman-compose 1.0.6):
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y podman podman-compose
sudo systemctl enable --now podman.socket   # rootful socket at /run/podman/podman.sock
Then tell AppBay which client to invoke:
appbay init --container-runtime podman






Notecontainer_runtime selects the CLIENT BINARY, not the daemon



docker here can perfectly well be talking to a rootful podman.socket via DOCKER_HOST — that is the documented and often preferable arrangement, since podman’s own man page notes docker-compose takes precedence as a compose provider when installed. Choose podman only when you want the podman binary itself invoked.





🚨 A version banner is not proof the runtime works. Measured: podman 6.0.2 with docker-compose v5.1.2 prints its version happily and then fails up with no such image on an image podman is holding. That reproduces with podman compose directly, with AppBay uninvolved.
docker run --rm hello-world          # or: sudo podman run --rm quay.io/podman/hello
If that does not print a success message, stop here. Nothing below will work, and the failure will surface later as something that looks like an AppBay bug.










Expectation
Why




:80 and :443 free
The edge binds both. One host runs exactly ONE edge — Traefik or Caddy — because they cannot share those ports.


A wildcard DNS record, or hosts entries
*.your.domain must reach this host. For a local TLD, per-client /etc/hosts entries work.


Outbound 443 for ACME
Only if you want real certificates. A local TLD uses a self-signed wildcard cert instead and needs no outbound access.



⚠️ If something else already holds :80 or :443, the edge container starts and immediately exits, and compose up -d reports success for that — it started a container, it does not wait to see whether it stays up. Check first:
sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E ':80 |:443 '




doctor runs every prerequisite and health check and reports pass/fail per check with an actionable fix for each failure. It is the first thing to run on a fresh host.
appbay doctor
Expected output (healthy host):
Appbay Doctor

  ✓ Platform
    Linux (Docker Engine)
  ✓ Docker
    Docker version 29.4.0, build 9d7ad9f
  ✓ Docker service
    server v29.4.0
  ✓ Docker Compose v2
    v5.1.2
  ✓ Compose >= 2.23.1
    v5.1.2
  ✓ APPBAY_HOME
    /home/appbay/.appbay
  ✓ appbay_shared network
    exists
  ✓ Shared network DNS
    container on appbay_shared resolved a sibling by name
  ✓ Healthcheck start_period
    no known-slow app has an undersized start_period
  ...
  All required checks passed.


For AI operators and automation, doctor --json emits a flat envelope:
appbay doctor --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "checks": [
    { "name": "Docker", "passed": true, "detail": "Docker version 29.4.0", "required": true },
    { "name": "APPBAY_HOME", "passed": false, "detail": "/home/appbay/.appbay does not exist", "fix": "Run \"appbay init\" to create the Appbay home directory", "required": true }
  ]
}
ok is true only when every required check passed. Optional checks (GPU, vault, server, SOPS, etc.) do not affect ok — they are advisory.




Docker not found — the container runtime is not installed. On a RHEL-family host, run appbay init-system (step 2) to install it.
Docker service not responding — the daemon is installed but not running. Start it: sudo systemctl start docker.
Docker daemon is up but the current user cannot reach it without sudo — the daemon is running, but your user is not in the docker group (rootful Docker). The fix is group membership, not running appbay under sudo: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER, then log out and back in. appbay init-system does this for you.
APPBAY_HOME does not exist — expected on a fresh host; run appbay init (step 3).
appbay_shared network not found — run appbay init to create it.
Shared network DNS failed — a container on the shared network could not resolve a sibling by name. Recreate the network: docker network rm appbay_shared, then appbay init.




There are two deployment models, and the identity answer differs:









Model
Who runs appbay
Why
What appbay must NOT do




Standalone host (appbay init-system)
the operator’s user, no sudo
init-system adds the user to the container group
create system accounts / set ACLs (that’s init-system’s one-time job)


DGX fleet (Ansible)
root, via Ansible become: true
Ansible drives it; the tree is owned by the llmsvc service account (uid 950)
create system accounts / set ACLs — Ansible creates the D-6 uid model, appbay consumes it as data



The rule that holds in both models is not “never sudo” — it is that appbay never creates system accounts or sets ACLs. That is Ansible’s job on the fleet, and init-system’s one-time job on a standalone host. Folding uid/ACL creation into the CLI would escalate the whole tool.
So the two things doctor checks are:

Is the container binary installed? (docker --version) — no daemon, no sudo.
Can the current user reach the daemon without sudo? (docker info) — this is where sudo would otherwise creep in.

If check 2 fails because the daemon needs sudo, the fix is to join the container group (sudo usermod -aG docker $USER + re-login), which is exactly what appbay init-system sets up on a standalone host. On an Ansible-managed fleet, Ansible arranges access.




init-system is a standalone-host convenience for a single binary on a fresh box. It installs the container runtime, creates the appbay user/group, grants that account access to the runtime, creates $APPBAY_HOME and sets ownership + default ACLs on it, and installs the control-plane systemd unit.

Boundary: For the DGX fleet, ansible is authoritative. init-system is tested to work, but the fleet path is ansible substrate, not this command. It is RHEL-family-first (matches prod); Debian-family and other distros are detected but not bootstrapped.

Preview what would change without touching the host:
appbay init-system --dry-run
Appbay init-system

  Distro: Fedora Linux 43 (Cloud Edition) (rhel)
  Owner model: service account (D-6)
  APPBAY_HOME: /var/lib/appbay

  Dry run — would make these changes:

  • Create system group appbay
    sudo groupadd --system appbay
  • Create no-login system service account appbay (uid 950)
    sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --home-dir /var/lib/appbay --shell /usr/sbin/nologin --uid 950 --gid appbay appbay
  • Grant appbay the rootful Podman socket (SocketGroup on podman.socket)
  • Let appbay traverse /run/podman (tmpfiles override)
  • Create /var/lib/appbay
  • Set ownership on /var/lib/appbay to appbay:appbay (setgid 2770)
  • Set default ACLs on /var/lib/appbay (appbay:rwx, other::---)
  • Record the appbay home in /etc/appbay/config
  • Install /etc/systemd/system/appbay-server.service (not enabled — see the summary)

  No changes made.
On a Docker host the two Podman lines are replaced by a single sudo usermod -aG docker appbay.
Apply it (requires sudo):
appbay init-system


The appbay account gets root-equivalent control of this host’s containers. That is true on Docker and on Podman, by the same reasoning: anything that can drive the container runtime can start a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem. It is inherent to running a control plane as a non-root account, not something either mechanism adds.









how
what it is




Docker
usermod -aG docker appbay
the docker group on a root:docker 0660 daemon socket


Podman
SocketGroup=appbay on podman.socket, plus a tmpfiles override so the account can traverse /run/podman
the same grant, expressed on the socket rather than found on it — Podman ships no group with those semantics









Important



Podman here means the ROOTFUL socket, deliberately. Rootless is not a supported control-plane model: the edge binds :80 and :443, which a rootless container cannot do without setting net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start host-wide — a larger privilege change than granting one account one socket. The unit therefore sets CONTAINER_HOST=unix:///run/podman/podman.sock; without it podman run by a non-root user silently falls back to rootless and the grant does nothing. Rootless Podman for deployed apps is a separate question and is unaffected.


The two Podman files are declarations systemd re-applies itself, so the grant survives a socket restart and a reboot:

/etc/systemd/system/podman.socket.d/10-appbay.conf
/etc/tmpfiles.d/zz-appbay-podman.conf

A one-off setfacl on the socket would not: systemd recreates it on every start of podman.socket, and the ACL was on the old inode.
The command is idempotent: re-running it after a successful bootstrap reports Host is already bootstrapped. Nothing to do. Each step detects the current state and only changes what differs.




Unsupported distro family "debian" — init-system is RHEL-family-first. Install Docker manually, or use the ansible substrate for the DGX fleet.
sudo: setfacl: command not found — the acl package is absent on a minimal image. init-system falls back to chown -R appbay:appbay on the home directory automatically.
Executable not found in $PATH: "docker" on a Podman host — the runtime is recorded by appbay init --container-runtime podman, not by init-system. APPBAY_CONTAINER_RUNTIME is a one-invocation override and does not persist.
statfs /run/user/<uid>/podman/podman.sock: no such file or directory — the install predates the rootful grant. Re-run appbay init-system, which writes the CONTAINER_HOST the unit needs.
appbay doctor says the service account cannot reach the runtime — run appbay init-system. Doctor prints the exact command it used; run that to see the underlying error.





init creates the $APPBAY_HOME directory structure, the shared Docker network, seeds system-app definitions, and writes the server compose file. It is idempotent and resumable.
appbay init --project homelab --domain homelab.example.com --yes
init runs a preflight gate first: it verifies the environment-level required checks (runtime present, service reachable, Compose v2, Compose version). If any fails, it prints the failures + fixes and aborts:
Preflight check failed — cannot initialize Appbay:

  ✗ Docker
    Docker not found
    Fix: Install Docker: https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/  (or run "appbay init-system" on a RHEL-family host to install it)

Appbay runs as your user, not root. If a check says the daemon needs sudo,
add your user to the container group (or run "appbay init-system") rather
than running appbay under sudo.

Fix the issues above, then re-run. Or use --force to continue anyway.
Use --force to skip the gate and continue anyway (not recommended — a host without Docker cannot run Appbay).









Flag
Purpose




--dir <path>
custom APPBAY_HOME (default ~/.appbay)


--project <name>
project name


--domain <name>
base domain for ingress routing


--container-runtime <docker\|podman>
container binary to invoke


--ingress-provider <traefik\|caddy>
reverse proxy to emit config for


--refresh-system-apps
replace drifted system-app files (.bak kept)


--force
skip the preflight gate







Preflight gate aborts — fix the reported environment issue, or pass --force. See the doctor failure modes above.
Docker network "appbay_shared" already exists — expected on re-init; init is idempotent.





setup is the guided wizard. It calls init internally, then initializes the secrets vault and deploys the selected edge (Traefik or integrated Caddy Security).
appbay setup
For scripting or CI, pass all options as flags:
appbay setup --domain homelab.example.com --project homelab --ingress-provider caddy --yes
At the end it prints bootstrap credentials for the admin user.

Check

docker --version

v2.23.1+

AppBay never installs packages, invokes sudo, or mutates host services and firewall policy; appbay doctor reports what is missing and names the repair step, and stops there.
Measured on Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker 29.1.3, Compose v2.40.3):
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y docker.io docker-compose-v2
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"      # log out and back in for this to take effect

Measured on Ubuntu 24.04 (Podman 4.9.3, podman-compose 1.0.6):
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y podman podman-compose
sudo systemctl enable --now podman.socket   # rootful socket at /run/podman/podman.sock
Then tell AppBay which client to invoke:
appbay init --container-runtime podman






Notecontainer_runtime selects the CLIENT BINARY, not the daemon



docker here can perfectly well be talking to a rootful podman.socket via DOCKER_HOST — that is the documented and often preferable arrangement, since podman’s own man page notes docker-compose takes precedence as a compose provider when installed. Choose podman only when you want the podman binary itself invoked.





🚨 A version banner is not proof the runtime works. Measured: podman 6.0.2 with docker-compose v5.1.2 prints its version happily and then fails up with no such image on an image podman is holding. That reproduces with podman compose directly, with AppBay uninvolved.
docker run --rm hello-world          # or: sudo podman run --rm quay.io/podman/hello
If that does not print a success message, stop here. Nothing below will work, and the failure will surface later as something that looks like an AppBay bug.










Expectation
Why




:80 and :443 free
The edge binds both. One host runs exactly ONE edge — Traefik or Caddy — because they cannot share those ports.


A wildcard DNS record, or hosts entries
*.your.domain must reach this host. For a local TLD, per-client /etc/hosts entries work.


Outbound 443 for ACME
Only if you want real certificates. A local TLD uses a self-signed wildcard cert instead and needs no outbound access.



⚠️ If something else already holds :80 or :443, the edge container starts and immediately exits, and compose up -d reports success for that — it started a container, it does not wait to see whether it stays up. Check first:
sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E ':80 |:443 '

doctor runs every prerequisite and health check and reports pass/fail per check with an actionable fix for each failure. It is the first thing to run on a fresh host.
appbay doctor
Expected output (healthy host):
Appbay Doctor

    Linux (Docker Engine)
  ✓ Docker

For AI operators and automation, doctor --json emits a flat envelope:
appbay doctor --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "checks": [
    { "name": "Docker", "passed": true, "detail": "Docker version 29.4.0", "required": true },
    { "name": "APPBAY_HOME", "passed": false, "detail": "/home/appbay/.appbay does not exist", "fix": "Run \"appbay init\" to create the Appbay home directory", "required": true }
  ]
}
ok is true only when every required check passed. Optional checks (GPU, vault, server, SOPS, etc.) do not affect ok — they are advisory.




Docker not found — the container runtime is not installed. On a RHEL-family host, run appbay init-system (step 2) to install it.
Docker service not responding — the daemon is installed but not running. Start it: sudo systemctl start docker.
Docker daemon is up but the current user cannot reach it without sudo — the daemon is running, but your user is not in the docker group (rootful Docker). The fix is group membership, not running appbay under sudo: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER, then log out and back in. appbay init-system does this for you.
APPBAY_HOME does not exist — expected on a fresh host; run appbay init (step 3).
appbay_shared network not found — run appbay init to create it.
Shared network DNS failed — a container on the shared network could not resolve a sibling by name. Recreate the network: docker network rm appbay_shared, then appbay init.




There are two deployment models, and the identity answer differs:









Model
Who runs appbay
Why
What appbay must NOT do




Standalone host (appbay init-system)
the operator’s user, no sudo
init-system adds the user to the container group
create system accounts / set ACLs (that’s init-system’s one-time job)


DGX fleet (Ansible)
root, via Ansible become: true
Ansible drives it; the tree is owned by the llmsvc service account (uid 950)
create system accounts / set ACLs — Ansible creates the D-6 uid model, appbay consumes it as data



The rule that holds in both models is not “never sudo” — it is that appbay never creates system accounts or sets ACLs. That is Ansible’s job on the fleet, and init-system’s one-time job on a standalone host. Folding uid/ACL creation into the CLI would escalate the whole tool.
So the two things doctor checks are:

Is the container binary installed? (docker --version) — no daemon, no sudo.
Can the current user reach the daemon without sudo? (docker info) — this is where sudo would otherwise creep in.

If check 2 fails because the daemon needs sudo, the fix is to join the container group (sudo usermod -aG docker $USER + re-login), which is exactly what appbay init-system sets up on a standalone host. On an Ansible-managed fleet, Ansible arranges access.

title: Bootstrap Guide
text:
init-system is a standalone-host convenience for a single binary on a fresh box. It installs the container runtime, creates the appbay user/group, grants that account access to the runtime, creates $APPBAY_HOME and sets ownership + default ACLs on it, and installs the control-plane systemd unit.

Boundary: For the DGX fleet, ansible is authoritative. init-system is tested to work, but the fleet path is ansible substrate, not this command. It is RHEL-family-first (matches prod); Debian-family and other distros are detected but not bootstrapped.

Preview what would change without touching the host:
appbay init-system --dry-run
Appbay init-system

  Distro: Fedora Linux 43 (Cloud Edition) (rhel)
  Owner model: service account (D-6)
  APPBAY_HOME: /var/lib/appbay

  Dry run — would make these changes:

  • Create system group appbay
    sudo groupadd --system appbay
  • Create no-login system service account appbay (uid 950)
    sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --home-dir /var/lib/appbay --shell /usr/sbin/nologin --uid 950 --gid appbay appbay
  • Grant appbay the rootful Podman socket (SocketGroup on podman.socket)
  • Let appbay traverse /run/podman (tmpfiles override)
  • Create /var/lib/appbay
  • Set ownership on /var/lib/appbay to appbay:appbay (setgid 2770)
  • Set default ACLs on /var/lib/appbay (appbay:rwx, other::---)
  • Record the appbay home in /etc/appbay/config
  • Install /etc/systemd/system/appbay-server.service (not enabled — see the summary)

  No changes made.
On a Docker host the two Podman lines are replaced by a single sudo usermod -aG docker appbay.
Apply it (requires sudo):
appbay init-system


The appbay account gets root-equivalent control of this host’s containers. That is true on Docker and on Podman, by the same reasoning: anything that can drive the container runtime can start a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem. It is inherent to running a control plane as a non-root account, not something either mechanism adds.









how
what it is




Docker
usermod -aG docker appbay
the docker group on a root:docker 0660 daemon socket


Podman
SocketGroup=appbay on podman.socket, plus a tmpfiles override so the account can traverse /run/podman
the same grant, expressed on the socket rather than found on it — Podman ships no group with those semantics









Important



Podman here means the ROOTFUL socket, deliberately. Rootless is not a supported control-plane model: the edge binds :80 and :443, which a rootless container cannot do without setting net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start host-wide — a larger privilege change than granting one account one socket. The unit therefore sets CONTAINER_HOST=unix:///run/podman/podman.sock; without it podman run by a non-root user silently falls back to rootless and the grant does nothing. Rootless Podman for deployed apps is a separate question and is unaffected.


The two Podman files are declarations systemd re-applies itself, so the grant survives a socket restart and a reboot:

/etc/systemd/system/podman.socket.d/10-appbay.conf
/etc/tmpfiles.d/zz-appbay-podman.conf

A one-off setfacl on the socket would not: systemd recreates it on every start of podman.socket, and the ACL was on the old inode.
The command is idempotent: re-running it after a successful bootstrap reports Host is already bootstrapped. Nothing to do. Each step detects the current state and only changes what differs.




Unsupported distro family "debian" — init-system is RHEL-family-first. Install Docker manually, or use the ansible substrate for the DGX fleet.
sudo: setfacl: command not found — the acl package is absent on a minimal image. init-system falls back to chown -R appbay:appbay on the home directory automatically.
Executable not found in $PATH: "docker" on a Podman host — the runtime is recorded by appbay init --container-runtime podman, not by init-system. APPBAY_CONTAINER_RUNTIME is a one-invocation override and does not persist.
statfs /run/user/<uid>/podman/podman.sock: no such file or directory — the install predates the rootful grant. Re-run appbay init-system, which writes the CONTAINER_HOST the unit needs.
appbay doctor says the service account cannot reach the runtime — run appbay init-system. Doctor prints the exact command it used; run that to see the underlying error.

than running appbay under sudo.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Conditional overlays are Compose fragments that are merged into an app’s configuration only when specified conditions are met. The condition is which apps are installed – enabling automatic cross-app wiring without manual configuration.
For example, Open WebUI can connect to Ollama when Ollama is installed alongside it, and fall back to a standalone configuration when it is not. This is declared once and evaluated automatically at compile time.






Importantwhen: means installed, not running



A when clause asks whether a peer app is declared in this installation – a fact about your desired state. It does not ask the container runtime anything, so it is the same answer whether Docker is up, down, or absent, and whether the peer is healthy, restarting or stopped.
This changed in v0.0.1-alpha.12. Overlays previously evaluated against a docker ps snapshot taken at compile time, which meant a restart-looping peer satisfied a clause, a stopped peer silently removed configuration, and a compile on a host with no Docker daemon deactivated every overlay while still reporting success.

For example, Open WebUI can connect to Ollama when Ollama is installed alongside it, and fall back to a standalone configuration when it is not. This is declared once and evaluated automatically at compile time.

Overlays previously evaluated against a docker ps snapshot taken at compile time, which meant a restart-looping peer satisfied a clause, a stopped peer silently removed configuration, and a compile on a host with no Docker daemon deactivated every overlay while still reporting success.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Basic syntax
Overlays are declared in the overlays section of appbay.yaml:
# apps/webui/appbay.yaml
overlays:
  - when: [ollama]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434
The when clause specifies which apps must be installed. The services block is a standard Compose fragment that gets merged into the app’s rendered output.

How service names work in overlays
When referencing a service from another app in an overlay, use the shared network alias format: <app>_<service> (underscore). In the example above, ollama_web refers to the web service of the ollama app, as aliased on the shared network.
If the app declares a namespace:, the alias gains it as a leading segment – <namespace>_<app>_<service> – and any dots in the namespace become hyphens, because a dot separates labels in DNS and would split the alias into two names that resolve to nothing. So an app in namespace uom.sim publishes uom-sim_litellm_web. Apps without a namespace, which is the default, are unaffected: the alias stays <app>_<service>.
This is because each app runs in its own Compose project with an internal network. Cross-app communication happens through the shared network, where exposed services are aliased with their app name prefix.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
The when clause

AND condition (array)
A plain array means all listed apps must be installed:
overlays:
  - when: [ollama, tts]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434
          - TTS_URL=http://tts_web:5000
This overlay only applies when both ollama and tts are installed.


OR condition ({any: []})
Use the any key for OR logic – the overlay applies when at least one of the listed apps is installed:
overlays:
  - when:
      any: [ollama, llamacpp, vllm]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - LLM_AVAILABLE=true
This overlay applies when any of ollama, llamacpp, or vllm is installed.


Combining conditions with multiple overlays
when supports either AND (array of strings) or OR (any: object) in a single clause – not both at once. To require both conditions, use two separate overlays:
overlays:
  # Requires caddy (the auth edge) to be installed
  - when: [caddy]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - AUTH_ENABLED=true

  # Requires at least one LLM backend to be installed
  - when:
      any: [ollama, llamacpp]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - LLM_AVAILABLE=true
Both overlays are evaluated independently. If only caddy is installed, only AUTH_ENABLED is injected. If both conditions are met, both fragments are merged.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Overlay evaluation
Overlays are evaluated during the compile step, before traits are applied. The evaluation follows these rules:

The installed app set is every app declared in this installation – the full contents of $APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps. It is not narrowed by the apps you name on the command line.
For each app being compiled, its overlays are checked against that set.
If a when clause is satisfied, the services fragment is deep-merged into the app’s Compose model.
Multiple matching overlays are applied in declaration order.
After all overlays are merged, traits are applied on top.







NoteTargeting an app does not change what it renders



appbay up webui and appbay up produce the same rendered output for webui, because the installed set is the whole installation either way. Narrowing the command line narrows what gets deployed, never what gets compiled into it.







flowchart TD
    A[Read installed apps] --> B[For each app]
    B --> C{Check when clause}
    C -->|satisfied| D[Deep-merge services fragment]
    C -->|not satisfied| E[Skip overlay]
    D --> F{More overlays?}
    E --> F
    F -->|yes| C
    F -->|no| G[Apply traits]

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Cross-app wiring examples

Ollama and Open WebUI
# apps/webui/appbay.yaml
overlays:
  - when: [ollama]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434
        depends_on:
          ollama-proxy:
            condition: service_started

  - when: [tts]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - AUDIO_TTS_ENGINE=openai
          - AUDIO_TTS_OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://tts_web:8000/v1
When both Ollama and TTS are installed, both overlays apply and the WebUI is wired to both services.


Authentication for multiple apps
Authentication is applied per-app with the auth trait (see Traits), not through overlays. Each app that needs login declares an auth trait, and the Caddy Security edge generates the authorization policy for it. Overlays are for conditional environment wiring, not for attaching auth middleware.


Database wiring
# apps/gitea/appbay.yaml
overlays:
  - when: [postgres]
    services:
      server:
        environment:
          - GITEA__database__DB_TYPE=postgres
          - GITEA__database__HOST=postgres_db:5432
          - GITEA__database__NAME=gitea
        depends_on:
          postgres-proxy:
            condition: service_healthy

  # Fallback: use built-in SQLite when no shared postgres
  # (This is the default when the overlay does not apply)

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Overlay merge behavior
The services block in an overlay is deep-merged into the base compose using these rules:

environment, volumes, ports (arrays): appended — overlay entries follow base entries; Docker Compose uses the last definition for duplicate keys
labels, depends_on (objects): shallow-merged — overlay values override base values on key collision
Scalars (image, command, etc.): overlay value replaces base
Services are merged by name (not replaced); adding a key to an existing service, or a new service entirely, both work


Override vs append
If the base compose already defines OLLAMA_BASE_URL and the overlay also sets it, the overlay value wins:
# Base compose
services:
  web:
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434   # default fallback

# Overlay (when ollama is installed)
services:
  web:
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434   # overrides the default

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Multiple overlays
An app can have multiple overlays. They are evaluated independently and applied in order:
overlays:
  # First overlay
  - when: [ollama]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434

  # Second overlay
  - when: [searxng]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - RAG_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE=searxng
          - SEARXNG_QUERY_URL=http://searxng_web:8080

  # Third overlay (OR condition)
  - when:
      any: [whisper, faster-whisper]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - AUDIO_STT_ENGINE=openai
If all three conditions are met, all three fragments are merged. If only Ollama is installed, only the first overlay applies.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Inspecting overlay state

CLI
appbay status webui
The output lists declared overlays and which services each affects:
  Overlays (3):
    - when all: [ollama] -> services: web
    - when all: [searxng] -> services: web
    - when any: [whisper, faster-whisper] -> services: web
appbay status is offline-capable – it reads from the appbay.yaml definition and does not require the server to be running. It lists all declared overlays without an active/inactive distinction.


Web UI
The App Detail screen shows overlay activation state in the overlays panel, with visual indicators for active (green) and inactive (gray) overlays. It evaluates the same installed set the compiler does, so the panel and the rendered output always agree.

title: Conditional Overlays
text:
Best practices
Keep overlays simple. An overlay should wire one integration concern. If you find yourself with complex nested logic, consider whether the app should use a different architecture.
Use overlays for optional dependencies, not required ones. If an app cannot function without another app, use depends_on in the base compose, not an overlay.
Name services consistently. Since shared network aliases follow the <app>_<service> pattern (underscore), use predictable service names like web, api, db to make cross-app references readable.
Test without overlays. Compile myapp in an installation where its peers are not installed to verify the base configuration works standalone. Stopping a peer’s containers will not do it – the peer is still installed, so the overlay still applies.

title: Core Concepts
text:
Appbay is inspired by the Open Application Model (OAM) – a specification for describing cloud-native applications. OAM separates the concerns of application developers, platform operators, and infrastructure providers. Appbay adapts these ideas for single-node Docker Compose deployments.
The central idea: Docker Compose is the application model. Your docker-compose.yml file is the component definition. Appbay adds traits, scopes, and policies on top – without replacing Compose.

title: Core Concepts
text:
Apps
An app is a directory under $APPBAY_HOME/etc/apps/ containing a docker-compose.yml file. The directory name is the app name. No configuration file is needed to register an app – just create the directory.
etc/apps/
  ollama/
    docker-compose.yml       # required
    appbay.yaml              # optional -- only if you need traits, overlays, or scope
  jellyfin/
    docker-compose.yml
    appbay.yaml
  whoami/
    docker-compose.yml
An app can contain multiple Compose services. For example, a nextcloud app might have services for the web server, the database, and a Redis cache. Appbay treats the entire directory as one deployable unit.

title: Core Concepts
text:
Services
A service is a Docker Compose service within an app. Appbay does not redefine what a service is – it uses the standard Compose service model. Traits can be applied at the service level (e.g., ingress on a specific service) or at the app level (e.g., backup for the entire app).

title: Core Concepts
text:
Traits
A trait is a reusable, declarative transformation that adds or modifies behavior. Traits are attached to apps or services in appbay.yaml and are applied during compilation.
Appbay v1 ships with seven core traits:








Trait
Scope
Purpose




ingress
service
Traefik/Caddy routing, TLS, exposure modes


gpu
service
GPU device passthrough (Nvidia/CDI/ROCm)


auth
app
Caddy Security browser login and role-based authorization


hooks
service
Init containers, sidecars, config injection


scoped-env
app
Variable injection from project/environment scopes


secrets
service
URI-based secret resolution


backup
app
Scheduled backup with retention policy



Traits follow OAM rules:

Applied in declaration order. The order you list traits matters.
One configuration per trait type per service. You cannot attach two ingress traits to the same service.
Conflict declarations. Some traits declare conflictsWith to prevent incompatible combinations.

See Traits for detailed documentation of each trait.

title: Core Concepts
text:
Scopes
Appbay has three organizational concepts that control different aspects of the runtime:





flowchart LR
    P[Project] -->|variable namespace| V1[project.yaml vars]
    E[Environment] -->|variable values| V2[environment.yaml vars]
    E -->|cert selection| TLS[staging vs production]

container_runtime and ingress_provider are set through appbay init, which applies them on re-init too and reports created / updated / unchanged:

Who the edge lets in
By default the Caddy edge has a single local identity store — the accounts appbay edge users manages, hashed into etc/apps/caddy/config/security/users.json. edge_identity: replaces that with a directory or an OIDC provider, at which point appbay stores no human password at all: what remains is one bind password or client secret, a vault:// reference like any other.
# $APPBAY_HOME/etc/system.yaml
edge_identity:
  providers:
    - type: local            # keep a break-glass local account
      realm: local
    - type: ldap
      realm: corp
      servers: ["ldaps://dc1.corp.example.com"]
      bindDn: "CN=svc-appbay,OU=Service,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com"
      bindPasswordRef: "vault://caddy/LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD"
      searchBaseDn: "DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com"
      searchUserFilter: "(&(sAMAccountName=%s)(objectclass=user))"
      groupRoleMap:
        "CN=AppBay-Admins,OU=Groups,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com": ["authp/admin"]
appbay init renders this into the edge’s Caddyfile and adds bindPasswordRef to caddy’s secrets trait, so the credential travels the ordinary secret path and never reaches a file on disk. Omitting the key is the single local store — byte for byte the configuration every installation has always had, so adding nothing changes nothing.
⚠️ Provider order is load-bearing. Caddy Security tries them in the order listed and the first is the portal’s default store, so a broad provider listed first shadows a narrower one after it.
⚠️ An oidc provider couples edge start-up to the IdP. Caddy Security fetches the issuer metadata and the signing keys while provisioning, so an unreachable IdP fails the whole edge rather than degrading logins. Keeping a local provider in the list is the break-glass path.


Reaching the control plane through the edge
appbay server start writes a Caddy site block for the control plane itself, so the web UI is reachable at appbay.<domain> behind the same login portal as every other app — and behind an admin-only policy, because it is the one stack that can reach the container runtime socket. Set server_host: to serve it somewhere else.
Nothing is written when the installation runs Traefik (the auth portal is Caddy Security only) or when there is no domain: and no server_host: — a local install has no name to serve it at, and that is normal rather than an error.
When that route is written, appbay server start also binds port 3000 to loopback, so the edge becomes the only way in from the network. Without a route it stays on all interfaces — closing the port when there is nowhere else to go in is a lockout, not a hardening.

⚠️ The web UI still checks its own password. Handing authentication to the edge is the rest of RFC-001 §1; the loopback bind is its precondition, because with the port open on every interface, trusting an identity the edge forwards in a header would let anyone who can reach 3000 set that header themselves.

RFC-001 §2.1 renamed the installation config to etc/system.yaml, because the two shared nothing but a name and the root one held no project-scoped keys at all.

Project
A namespace disambiguates one copy of an app from another on the same host. It is a label, not a variable scope: it does not select a variable file, and ${{project.KEY}} does not read it. That reference resolves against the installation config above, which is one file per host shared by every namespace on it — see Scope Model.
# appbay.yaml
namespace: homelab
Container, network and shared-alias names derive from the app name and the namespace when one is declared. Without a namespace — the default — containers are appbay.<app>.<service>, volumes are prefixed <app>_, and apps join appbay_shared (or whatever shared_network specifies). With namespace: homelab, the container becomes appbay.homelab.<app>.<service> and the shared alias homelab_<app>_<service>, so two namespaces of one app do not collide.
Dots in a namespace become hyphens wherever the name reaches a hostname, because a dot separates labels in DNS: namespace: uom.sim publishes uom-sim_<app>_<service>.
Use a namespace when you need two copies of an app side by side — homelab and work-lab get distinct containers, networks and shared aliases and never collide.
⚠️ They do not get distinct variables. There is one domain: per installation, so ${{project.DOMAIN}} is the same value in every namespace. Per-namespace variables are not implemented; use a plain Compose ${VAR} from the app’s .env for a value that must differ.


Environment
An environment is a deployment variant. It determines which variable values, secret URIs, and certificate resolvers are used.
# appbay.yaml
namespace: prod
project and environment were a single axis in disguise — every shipped manifest set both to default — so RFC-001 §4 collapsed them into one dot-delimited namespace. Typical values: prod (real domain, production certs), dev (localhost, staging certs), or a compound like uom.sim.
⚠️ There is no environment: field any more. It was removed with project: in RFC-001 §4 and the schema now accepts only the literal default for either, so an old manifest still parses and a manifest trying to use one fails loudly instead of being silently ignored. Put the variant in namespace: — namespace: uom.sim — and deploy a second copy alongside the first.


Collection
A collection is an operational grouping – a named set of apps that deploy, restart, or stop together. Collections are multi-valued and purely a selection mechanism.
# appbay.yaml
collection: [ai-stack, gpu-apps]
Usage: appbay up --collection ai-stack deploys all apps tagged with that collection.
Collections do not participate in variable resolution. They are selectors, not scope levels.

Core Concepts
text:
Overlays
Conditional overlays are Compose fragments that are applied only when specified conditions are met – typically when a peer app is active. This enables declarative cross-app wiring without manual configuration.
# apps/webui/appbay.yaml
overlays:
  - when: [ollama]
    services:
      web:
        environment:
          - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama_web:11434
When Appbay detects that ollama is in the active app set, it merges this fragment into WebUI’s rendered compose. See Conditional Overlays for full syntax.

title: Core Concepts
text:
How a deploy actually executes
There is no operator service. Whichever interface you used — CLI, web, or desktop — calls @appbay/core in its own process, which compiles your app, spawns the configured compose client, reports, and exits. Runtime capabilities (GPU availability, runtime version, disk, OS) are probed from the host during that run.
A deployed app keeps running after every Appbay process is gone. That is the design: Appbay is a deployer, not a supervisor.
In v1, there is a single operator co-located with the server. The operator field in appbay.yaml is optional and defaults to local. The architecture supports multiple operators on different nodes in future versions.





flowchart TD
    S[CLI / web / desktop] -->|in-process call| O["@appbay/core pipeline"]
    O -->|Docker Socket<br/>read-only mount| D[Docker Engine]
    O -->|reports| F[Runtime Facts<br/>GPU, disk, OS]
